facts.value: HMML counts more than 200,000 manuscripts from some 36 libraries in Timbuktu. Other figures on this site run higher, so treat the number as approximate.
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://hmml.org/stories/where-were-working-mali/' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'more than 200,000 from some 36 libraries'

facts.value: A rescue worker told HMML she showed photos of the 1,400 metal boxes used to carry Timbuktu manuscripts out.
facts.quote: She showed me photos of the 1,400 metal boxes
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://hmml.org/stories/a-decade-in-mali/' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'She showed me photos of the 1,400 metal boxes'

facts.value: Libraries that stayed in Timbuktu were hidden by their owners, as families had done when the Moroccans invaded in the late sixteenth century and the French in the nineteenth.

facts.value: The Mamma Haidara Family Library is one of the largest private manuscript collections in Timbuktu. Some of its documents date to the 13th century.
